content_metadata.description: This video provides an educational overview of the internal foramina of a human skull, focusing on identifying and explaining their significance through a model demonstration.

qAndA.question: What is the large hole at the center of the skull base called?
Which foramen is located just above the foramen magnum on this view?
What important structure passes through the carotid canal?

qAndA.answer: The foramen ovale is situated posteriorly and laterally to the foramen rotundum.
qAndA.question: Where is the foramen ovale located relative to the foramen rotundum?

qAndA.answer: They serve as passageways for vital nerves and blood vessels that supply the head and neck.
qAndA.question: What is the significance of these foramina in the skull?
